presidentialSuccession.name: Lenín Moreno
presidentialSuccession.notes: Elected with PAIS but broke with Correa; governed from the centre-right.

supremeCourt.name: Corte Nacional de Justicia (and Corte Constitucional)
supremeCourt.appointmentMethod: Judges selected through a merit competition run by the Judicial Council (Consejo de la Judicatura).
supremeCourt.fspEraChanges: A 2011 referendum under Correa restructured the judiciary, creating a transitional Judicial Council that overhauled judge selection; critics said it gave the executive undue influence over appointments, supporters cited reform of a dysfunctional system.
supremeCourt.stillServing: Post-Correa governments have continued to reshape the Judicial Council and the courts; the bench turns over through the merit-competition mechanism. Current members not itemized here.

courtHistory.event: Amid recurrent instability the older Corte Suprema was repeatedly reshaped across military and civilian governments.
President Gutiérrez and his congressional allies dissolved and re-packed the Supreme Court (the 'Pichi Corte') — the move triggered the 2005 crisis that ousted him.
Correa's new Constitution replaced the Corte Suprema with the Corte Nacional de Justicia and created the Corte Constitucional.

A referendum restructured the judiciary via a transitional Consejo de la Judicatura that overhauled judge selection — critics said it gave the executive undue influence; supporters cited reform of a dysfunctional system.
Post-Correa governments (Moreno, Lasso, Noboa) reshaped the Judicial Council and the bench again through merit competitions.

supremeCourt.justicesNote: Judges are selected by merit competition via the Consejo de la Judicatura; the bench turns over and is not itemized here.
